subject: math2
loDesc: Understands undefined terms (point, line, plane), distance on a number line, betweenness property, conditional statements, converse, and direct/indirect geometric proofs.
hookDemo: Display three points A, B, and C on a line where d(A,B) = 3 and d(B,C) = 4.
hookAsk: Under what condition does d(A,C) equal 7, and what does this tell us about betweenness P-Q-R?
streamDo: Observe conditional statement: 'If a quadrilateral is a rhombus, then its diagonals are perpendicular.'
streamTask: Identify Given hypothesis and To Prove conclusion, then write the Converse statement.
mountainTask: Co-ordinates of points P and Q on a number line are -3 and 5 respectively. Find distance d(P, Q) using d(P,Q) = Larger co-ordinate - Smaller co-ordinate.
skyTask: Prove geometrically that vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are congruent.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming the converse of a true conditional statement is always automatically true.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If an animal is a dog, it has four legs (true). Is the converse "If an animal has four legs, it is a dog" also true?' Show counterexamples.

crossCurricularLinks: Logic & Philosophy: Formal Deduction (Structuring hypothesis-conclusion conditional proofs)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Understands fundamental axioms, conditional statements, and geometric proofs.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use number lines marked on classroom floors for physical distance walk-throughs.

subject: math2
loDesc: Verifies Interior Angle Theorem, Alternate Angle Theorem, Corresponding Angle Theorem, and tests for parallel lines using transversal angle relationships.
hookDemo: Use two parallel wooden bars cut by a transversal bar with a magnetic protractor.
hookAsk: If interior angles on one side of a transversal add up to 170°, why MUST the two lines intersect if extended?
streamDo: Observe transversal diagrams with marked angle pairs.
streamTask: Classify angle pairs as Alternate Interior, Corresponding, or Interior angles on the same side.
mountainTask: In a given figure with line l parallel to line m, if one alternate angle is (2x + 10)° and the other is (3x - 20)°, solve for x and calculate the angle.
skyTask: Prove that if two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the interior angles on either side of the transversal are supplementary (sum = 180°).

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinking that interior angles on the same side of a transversal are equal rather than supplementary.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Look at the two interior angles—one is acute and one is obtuse. Can an acute angle equal an obtuse angle?'

crossCurricularLinks: Architecture & Civil Drafting: Structural Frameworks (Checking parallel alignment in building trusses using transversal angle tests)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Proves theorems on parallel lines and applies transversal properties.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use paper tracing overlays to demonstrate corresponding angle congruence.

subject: math2
loDesc: Applies Theorem of Remote Interior Angles, Congruence of Triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS), Isosceles Triangle Theorem, 30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90° Triangle Theorems, and Median Properties.
hookDemo: Display a 30°-60°-90° set-square on the board.
hookAsk: Why is the side opposite to the 30° angle always EXACTLY half the length of the hypotenuse?
streamDo: Observe triangle ABC where exterior angle at C is 110° and remote interior angle A is 50°.
streamTask: Calculate the measure of remote interior angle B using Exterior Angle Theorem.
mountainTask: In right-angled triangle LMN, angle M = 90°, angle L = 30°, and hypotenuse LN = 12 cm. Find lengths of sides MN and LM.
skyTask: Prove that if two sides of a triangle are congruent, then the angles opposite to them are congruent.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, assuming the side opposite 60° is half the hypotenuse instead of the side opposite 30°.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which angle is smaller, 30° or 60°? Should the smaller angle face the shorter side (1/2 hyp) or longer side (√3/2 hyp)?'

crossCurricularLinks: Physics & Trigonometry: Force Vector Resolution (Resolving inclined forces into 30°-60°-90° component lengths)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Proves properties of triangles including isosceles and special right-angled triangle theorems.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Cut out set-square replicas to physically verify side ratios in 30-60-90 triangles.

subject: math2
loDesc: Constructs triangles given base, angle adjacent to base, and sum of remaining two sides; difference of remaining two sides; or perimeter and two base angles.
hookDemo: Draw a rough sketch of a triangle on the board showing Base = 6 cm, angle B = 60°, and AB + AC = 9 cm.
hookAsk: How does constructing a perpendicular bisector help locate the exact position of vertex A?
streamDo: Observe given parameters (Base, Base Angle, Sum/Difference/Perimeter).
streamTask: Classify 3 construction problems into Type 1 (Sum given), Type 2 (Difference given), or Type 3 (Perimeter given).
mountainTask: Write step-by-step instructions to construct triangle ABC in which BC = 6.3 cm, angle B = 75°, and AB + AC = 9 cm.
skyTask: Construct triangle PQR with perimeter 11 cm, angle Q = 60°, and angle R = 45°, justifying why the constructed sides sum to 11 cm.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Drawing the final triangle without constructing a rough sketch first, leading to incorrect arc intersections.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Where will your compass arc land if you don't know which side represents the sum segment?' Always draw a rough sketch.

crossCurricularLinks: Engineering Graphics: Geometric Surveying (Constructing land boundary triangles from baseline perimeter measurements)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Constructs triangles using compass and ruler based on given sum/difference/perimeter.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Emphasize drawing accurate rough sketches with marked parameters before compass work.

subject: math2
loDesc: Proves properties of Parallelogram, Rhombus, Rectangle, Square, and Trapezium; proves Midpoint Theorem and its converse.
hookDemo: Display a triangle with midpoints of two sides connected by a line segment parallel to the third side.
hookAsk: Why is the line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle always parallel to and half the length of the third side?
streamDo: Observe special quadrilaterals (Rectangle, Rhombus, Square, Parallelogram).
streamTask: Match quadrilateral names with unique diagonal properties (Diagonals equal, Diagonals bisect at 90°).
mountainTask: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are (3x - 4)° and (3x + 16)°. Find the measure of all four interior angles.
skyTask: Prove that the segment joining the midpoints of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half as long as it.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming that any four-sided figure with equal diagonals must be a square, ignoring rectangles.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Are adjacent sides equal in a rectangle? Are its diagonals equal?' Show that equal diagonals occur in rectangles too.

crossCurricularLinks: Carpentry & Industrial Design: Frame Rigidity (Using midpoint bracing and parallel linkage in structural frames)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Proves theorems on quadrilaterals and applies the Midpoint Theorem.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use paper folding to verify midpoint segment length relative to the base side.

subject: math2
loDesc: Proves theorems on circle chords (perpendicular from center bisects chord; congruent chords are equidistant from center) and constructs incircle and circumcircle of a triangle.
hookDemo: Construct the perpendicular bisectors of two chords in a circle using a chalkboard compass.
hookAsk: Where do the perpendicular bisectors of any two chords in a circle always intersect?
streamDo: Observe triangle constructions: Angle Bisectors intersection vs Perpendicular Bisectors intersection.
streamTask: Classify the concurrence point as Incenter (Incircle center) or Circumcenter (Circumcircle center).
mountainTask: A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the center of a circle. Calculate the radius of the circle using Pythagoras theorem.
skyTask: Prove that congruent chords of a circle are equidistant from the center of the circle.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing the Incircle (tangent to sides, center from angle bisectors) with the Circumcircle (passes through vertices, center from side bisectors).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'To draw a circle passing through 3 vertices, do you bisect the sides or the angles?'

crossCurricularLinks: Navigation & Civil Geometry: Center Detection (Finding the exact center of circular arches and roundabouts using chord bisectors)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Proves circle chord theorems and constructs incircles and circumcircles.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use transparent circular overlays to verify chord bisection properties.

subject: math2
loDesc: Understands Cartesian coordinate system, axes (X and Y), origin, quadrants, plots points (x, y), and identifies equations of lines parallel to axes.
hookDemo: Display a 2D Cartesian grid with 4 quadrants marked I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-).
hookAsk: In which quadrant does point (-3, -5) lie, and why are both coordinates negative?
streamTask: State the Quadrant or Axis on which each given point lies.
mountainTask: Write the equations of lines parallel to the X-axis at a distance of 5 units below it, and parallel to Y-axis at 3 units to the left.
skyTask: Plot points A(1,1), B(5,1), C(5,4), D(1,4) on a coordinate grid, join them in order, identify the polygon formed, and calculate its area.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Reversing x and y coordinates when plotting points (e.g. plotting (2, 5) as 2 units up on Y and 5 units right on X).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'In ordered pair (x, y), which axis comes first alphabetically?' Always walk along X before climbing Y.

crossCurricularLinks: Computer Graphics & Mapping: GIS & Screen Pixels (Mapping 2D screen coordinates and GPS spatial positioning)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Plots points on Cartesian plane and understands linear equations parallel to axes.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use floor grid tiles for human coordinate plotting activities.

subject: math2
loDesc: Defines trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan) in right-angled triangles, understands trigonometric identities, and uses standard values (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°).
hookDemo: Display a right-angled triangle with acute angle theta, showing Opposite, Adjacent, and Hypotenuse sides.
hookAsk: Why is the ratio Opposite / Hypotenuse defined as sine theta, and how does it change as theta increases?
streamDo: Observe right triangle ABC right-angled at B with acute angle A.
streamTask: Write ratios for sin A, cos A, and tan A in terms of side lengths AB, BC, AC.
mountainTask: Evaluate the value of 2*sin(30°) + cos(60°) + 3*tan(45°) using standard trigonometric ratio tables.
skyTask: Prove that sin(90 - theta) = cos theta and tan(90 - theta) = cot theta using a right-angled triangle.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Treating 'sin θ' as a multiplication of 'sin' times 'θ' rather than a single unified ratio function.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does "sin" have any mathematical meaning without an angle θ attached to it?'

crossCurricularLinks: Physics & Surveying: Height & Distance Measurement (Using tan θ and sin θ to calculate building heights and ramp angles)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Understands trigonometric ratios in right-angled triangles and evaluates standard trigonometric values.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use right triangle set-squares to measure sides and verify sin/cos ratios.

subject: math2
loDesc: Calculates Total Surface Area, Curved Surface Area, and Volume of Cuboid, Cube, Right Circular Cylinder, Cone, and Sphere/Hemisphere.
hookDemo: Display 3D solid models: Cone, Cylinder, and Sphere of identical radius and height.
hookAsk: How many full cones of water does it take to completely fill a cylinder of the same base radius and height?
streamTitle: Surface Area vs Volume Formula Matching
streamDo: Observe 3D solids: Cone (r, h, l), Sphere (r), Cylinder (r, h).
streamTask: Match given 3D solids with their correct Curved Surface Area and Volume formulas.
mountainTask: Find the Curved Surface Area (pi*r*l) and Total Surface Area (pi*r*(r+l)) of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm.
skyTask: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small solid cones of radius 2 cm and height 3 cm. Calculate the number of cones formed.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing vertical height (h) with slant height (l) when calculating cone curved surface area (πrl).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'In CSA = πrl, is l measured along the sloped outer edge or straight down the vertical center?' Use l = √(r² + h²).

crossCurricularLinks: Industrial Packaging & Manufacturing: Material Efficiency (Calculating sheet metal requirements for cylindrical and conical containers)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Mathematics LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 76]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates surface area and volume of 3D solids including cones and spheres.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 6: Use water displacement in graduated cylinders to verify sphere volume formulas.
